claim_scope: Mechanism stress test; not FRANK hardware/data evidence and not a release-gate result.
hypothesis_tested: Unverified self-predictions used as online training truth create a positive-feedback contamination loop that worsens unknown rejection relative to sparse trusted-evidence updates.
model: 2D frozen representation with two drifting known classes and a moving unknown distribution; nearest-prototype classifier; Euclidean open-set threshold; exponential prototype updates.

policies.naive_self_update: Accept any sample inside threshold and update predicted prototype, including unknown samples misclassified as known.
policies.trust_gated: Only trusted labeled known examples update prototypes; unknown and self-generated labels never directly update trusted state.

interpretation: The synthetic mechanism reproduces the expected positive-feedback hazard: as OOD prevalence increases, an increasing fraction of accepted naive updates are actually unknown samples.
Unknown rejection degrades before known-class accuracy visibly collapses, so known accuracy alone is an insufficient health metric for an adaptive familiarity controller.
Sparse trusted updates preserve better unknown rejection in this setup, supporting the FRANK GOLD/SILVER admission rule as a control boundary worth testing in H1.
limitations: Synthetic low-dimensional geometry is not a substitute for real Retina embeddings.
Thresholds and distributions were chosen for mechanism discrimination, not to estimate production effect size.
The gated policy uses trusted labels; future H1 tests must model realistic GOLD/SILVER acquisition cost and imperfect SILVER evidence.
